Given that, $\arg \left(\frac{z-2}{z-6 i}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}$
\therefore \quad \arg (z-2)-\arg (z-6 i)=$\frac{\pi}{2}$Let $z=x+i y\begin{aligned}$& \Rightarrow \arg [(x-2)+i y]-\arg [x+i(y-6)]=$\frac{\pi}{2}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad \tan ^{-1} $\frac{y}{x-2}-\tan ^{-1} \frac{y-6}{x}=\frac{\pi}{2}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad\left(\frac{\frac{y}{x-2}-\frac{y-6}{x}}{1+\frac{y}{x-2} \cdot \frac{y-6}{x}}\right)=\tan \frac{\pi}{2}$\\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1+$\frac{y}{x-2} \cdot \frac{y-6}{x}=$0 \\
& \Rightarrow \quad x(x-2)+y(y-6)=0
\end{aligned} This is an equation of circle in diametric form.$

questions.q: The expression \left(\dfrac{1 + itan\alpha}{1 - itan\alpha}\right)n - \dfrac{1 + itann\alpha}{1 - itann\alpha}$ when simplified reduces to$
questions.solution:
Let& \left(\dfrac{1 + itan\alpha}{1 - itan\alpha}\right)n - \left(\dfrac{1 + itann\alpha}{1 - itann\alpha}\right) = z$

We know that~$tan\alpha = \dfrac{sin\alpha}{cos\alpha}$

$⇒ z = \left(\dfrac{cos\alpha + isin\alpha}{cos\alpha - isin\alpha}\right)n - \left(\dfrac{cosn\alpha + isinn\alpha}{cosn\alpha - isinn\alpha}\right)

From Euler formula, we get

$⇒ z = \left(\dfrac{ei\alpha}{e- i\alpha}\right)$n - $\dfrac{ein\alpha}{e- in\alpha}

$⇒ z = \left($e^{2i$\alpha}\right)n - e^{2in$\alpha}= e^{2in$\alpha} - e^{2in$\alpha} = 0$

$∴ \left(\dfrac{1 + itan\alpha}{1 - itan\alpha}\right)$n - $\dfrac{1 + itann\alpha}{1 - itann\alpha} =$0$

$

questions.q: Let $z$ and $w$ be non-zero complex numbers such that $zw = \left|z^{2}\right|$ and \left|z - \overset{-}{z}\right| + \left|w + \overset{-}{w}\right| = 4 .$ If $w$ varies, then the perimeter of the locus of $z$ is$
questions.solution:
Given, $zw = {\left|z\right|}^{2} ⇒ zw = z\overset{-}{z}$
$⇒ w = \overset{-}{z}\left\{z \ne 0\right\}$
Now, \left|z - \overset{-}{z}\right| + \left|w + \overset{-}{w}\right| = 4$
$⇒ \left|z - \overset{-}{z}\right| + \left|z + \overset{-}{z}\right| = 4$
Let, $z = x + iy$, then we get,
\left|x\right| + \left|y\right| = 2$
which represents a square of side length equal to $2\sqrt{2}$

$⇒$ The perimeter of the locus is $8\sqrt{2}$ units

We have, \left|$z+$\frac{i}{2}\right|^2=\left|$z-$\frac{i}{2}\right|^2 $\begin{array}{rlrl}

\Rightarrow & \left|$x+i\left($y+$\frac{1}{2}\right)\right|^2 & =\left|$x+i\left($y+$\frac{1}{2}\right)\right|^2 \\
\Rightarrow & x²+\left($y+$\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 & =x²+\left($y-$\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 \\
\Rightarrow & x²+y²+$\frac{1}{4}+$y & =x²+y²+$\frac{1}{4}-$y \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 y & =0 \\
\Rightarrow & y & =0
\end{array} Locus of $z$ is $x$-axis.

If $z$ and $\omega$ are two complex numbers such that \left|z\omega\right| = 1$ and $arg\left(z\right) - arg\left(\omega\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$, then $arg \left(\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega}\right)$is:
(Here $arg \left(z\right)$ denotes the principal argument of complex number $z$)$
questions.solution:
As

\left|z\omega\right| = 1$

If \left|z\right| = r$, then \left|\omega\right| = \dfrac{1}{r}$

Let $arg \left($z\right) = $\theta

$∴ arg\left(\omega\right) = \left(\theta - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)

So,

$z = re^{i$\theta}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{z} = re^{i \left(- \theta\right)}$
$⇒ $\omega = \dfrac{1}{r}$e^{i \left(\theta - \dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}$

Now, consider
\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega} = \dfrac{1 - 2e^{i \left(- $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}}{1 + 3e^{i \left(- $\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\right)}} = \left(\dfrac{1 - 2i}{1 + 3i}\right)$

$= \dfrac{ \left($1 - 2i\right)\left(1 - 3i\right)}${ \left($1 + 3i\right) \left($1 - 3i\right)} = \dfrac{1 - 5i + 6i^{2}}{10} = \dfrac{- 5 + 5i}{10} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\left($1 + i\right)$

Then,

$principalarg \left(\dfrac{1 - 2\overset{¯}{z}\omega}{1 + 3\overset{¯}{z}\omega}\right)

$= principalarg \left(- \dfrac{1}{2} \left($1 + i\right)\right)$

$= - \left(\pi - $\dfrac{π}{4}\right) = \dfrac{- 3\pi}{4}

questions.q: If z ≠ 1 and& $\dfrac{z^{2}}{\text{z} - 1}$& is real, then the point represented by the complex number z lies
options: Either on the real axis or on a circle not passing through the origin.
Either on the real axis or on a circle passing through the origin.
On a circle with centre at the origin.
questions.solution:
$\text{z} ≠ 1 \text{,} \dfrac{z^{2}}{\text{z} - 1}$~is real

If z is a real number, then $\dfrac{z^{2}}{\text{z} - 1}$~is real.

Let z = x + iy

$∴ \dfrac{\left(x^{2} - y^{2} + 2 \text{xiy}\right) \left(\left(\text{x} - 1\right) - \text{iy}\right)}{{\left(\text{x} - 1\right)}^{2} + y^{2}}$~equating imaginary part to zero.

$\to - \text{y} \left(x^{2} - y^{2}\right) + 2 \text{xy} \left(\text{x} - 1\right) = 0$

$\to \text{y} \left(x^{2} + y^{2} - 2 \text{x}\right) = 0 \to \text{y} = 0$~or~$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2 \text{x} = 0$

$∴$& z lies on real axis or on a circle passing through origin.
